threads.body: [Style] Tests should import incubating semantic-convention constants directly rather than recreate their keys. Using `GenAiIncubatingAttributes` here keeps this assertion tied to the canonical attribute names and types; the test dependency is already available in this module.

replies.body: Thanks. I tried this, but `:instrumentation-api-incubator:compileTestJava` rejects all three generated GenAI constants with `OtelDeprecatedApiUsage`. The production extractor intentionally defines these incubating keys locally, and this test mirrors that supported pattern. I’m keeping the local keys rather than suppressing the repository’s deprecated-API check.

threads.body: [Style] Test code should not add `@Nullable` annotations. These fields and constructor parameters are test fixtures, so leave them unannotated.

replies.body: Agreed. Removed `@Nullable` from the `Response` fixture fields and constructor parameters in f5a787e8; only the response reference passed to the getter remains nullable. The focused extractor test and `spotlessCheck` pass.

threads.body: `getUsageCacheReadInputTokens()` / `getUsageReasoningOutputTokens()` return `Long` (nullable), but the assertions compare against int literals (`12`, `4`) which are boxed as `Integer`. In AssertJ this can fail due to `Long(12)` not being equal to `Integer(12)`. Use `12L` / `4L` (or `isEqualTo(Long.valueOf(...))`) to match the returned type.

replies.body: Good point on making the numeric type explicit. AssertJ selects `LongAssert`, so the existing assertions were passing, but `12L` and `4L` communicate the getter’s return type more clearly. Updated in 760c4a7c; the focused OpenAI getter test passes.

threads.body: Visibility is inconsistent: existing attribute keys are `static final` with package-private visibility, while the newly added keys are `private static final`. This makes it harder for tests in the same package (or other internal code) to reuse the constants consistently (as seen by the test defining its own `longKey(...)` instances). Align the visibility with the existing constants unless there’s a specific reason to keep them private.

replies.body: Agreed. Changed the two new constants to package-private and reused them from the same-package extractor test in 760c4a7c. This matches the existing reusable extractor constants and avoids importing the generated GenAI constants, which this module rejects via `OtelDeprecatedApiUsage`. The focused extractor test passes.

threads.body: The fixture no longer provides `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` and `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`, but the updated OpenAI tests now expect `GEN_AI_USAGE_CACHE_READ_INPUT_TOKENS=0` and `GEN_AI_USAGE_REASONING_OUTPUT_TOKENS=0` for these scenarios. With this payload, the getter will return `null` for the detailed fields and the extractor will omit the corresponding attributes, causing those assertions to fail and/or undermining the “explicit zero values are still emitted” requirement. Consider restoring the detailed sub-objects with explicit zero values in this fixture (and keeping separate fixtures/tests for the “unavailable” case).

replies.body: I’m keeping this fixture without the detail objects. It is intentionally the end-to-end “source does not provide the value” case: `AbstractChatTest.basic()` expects the total input/output counts but does not expect either detailed attribute. Explicit-zero behavior is covered separately by fixtures such as `multiplechoices` and `streamincludeusage`, plus the shared extractor zero-value test. Restoring the detail objects here would remove the end-to-end omission coverage; the library and javaagent checks pass with this split.
